title: Sensory Exam & Dermatomes — Find the Level by Touch

hook.en: A numb thumb, a tingling calf, a loss of feeling at the belly button — each one points to a spinal level. Learn to test sensation properly and read the map without memorising it blindly.
hook.ur: Sunn angootha, jhunjhunati pindli, nabhi par ehsaas ka khatam hona — har ek kisi spinal level ki taraf ishara karta hai. Sensation sahi tareeqay se test karna aur map ko ratay bagair parhna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll test light touch and pinprick correctly, name the key points from C5 to S1, and tell a dermatome pattern from a nerve or glove-and-stocking pattern.
goal.ur: End tak aap light touch aur pinprick sahi test karenge, C5 se S1 tak key points batayenge, aur dermatome pattern ko nerve ya glove-and-stocking pattern se alag pehchan lenge.

text.en: A **dermatome** is the strip of skin supplied by one spinal nerve root. Think of the body as a long tube of skin with 30 stacked "ribbons", each wired to one level of the spinal cord. When a root is irritated or compressed (a disc, a bony spur, shingles), its ribbon goes numb, tingly or painful. So the sensory exam answers one question: **at which level is the problem?**
text.ur: **Dermatome** woh skin ki patti hai jisay ek spinal nerve root supply karti hai. Jism ko skin ki lambi nali samjhein jis par 30 “ribbons” ek ke upar ek lagi hain, har ek spinal cord ke ek level se jura hai. Jab koi root dab jaye ya irritate ho (disc, bony spur, shingles) to uski ribbon sunn, jhunjhuni wali ya dardnak ho jati hai. Is liye sensory exam ek hi sawal ka jawab deta hai: **masla kis level par hai?**

simpler.en: Each spinal root feeds one strip of skin. Numb strip = that root is in trouble.
simpler.ur: Har spinal root skin ki ek patti ko feed karti hai. Patti sunn = us root mein masla.

text.en: Dermatomes are like postal codes. The letter (touch signal) from your thumb always travels to the same sorting office (C6). If the sorting office is flooded (a compressed C6 root), every letter from that postal code is lost — and that is how you find the broken office from the missing letters.
text.ur: Dermatomes postal codes ki tarah hain. Aap ke angootay se chitthi (touch signal) hamesha ek hi sorting office (C6) jati hai. Agar sorting office mein sailab aa jaye (dabi hui C6 root) to us postal code ki har chitthi gum ho jati hai — aur gum chitthiyon se aap toota hua office dhoond lete hain.

beats.title: C6 dermatome — thumb and index finger

intro.en: Watch the **C6 zone glow** on the thumb side of the forearm, thumb and index finger. The glowing patch is where you would test. Press **Pause**, switch sides and compare.
intro.ur: **C6 zone** ko forearm ki thumb side, angootha aur index finger par roshan hota dekhein. Roshan hissa wohi hai jahan aap test karenge. **Pause** dabayein, side badlein aur compare karein.

text.en: **Hand trick:** hold your hand up. Thumb + index finger make a "6" → **C6**. Middle finger = **7** → **C7**. Little finger = **8** → **C8**. For the legs: **L4** is the inside of the ankle (the bump you stand on when kneeling), **L5** is the top of the foot and big toe, **S1** is the outer edge of the foot.
text.ur: **Haath ka trick:** haath upar karein. Thumb + index finger “6” banate hain → **C6**. Middle finger = **7** → **C7**. Little finger = **8** → **C8**. Taangon ke liye: **L4** ankle ka andar wala hissa, **L5** foot ka top aur bara angootha, **S1** foot ka bahar wala kinara.

question.en: A patient has numbness over the **little finger and the inner forearm**. Which root is most likely involved?
question.ur: Patient ki **little finger aur inner forearm** sunn hain. Kaun si root sab se zyada involved hai?

feedback.en: Yes — the little finger is the "8" of the hand trick and the inner forearm is the C8 ribbon. Also check finger flexors and grip.
feedback.ur: Haan — little finger hand trick ka “8” hai aur inner forearm C8 ki ribbon hai. Finger flexors aur grip bhi check karein.

feedback.en: C5 is the outer upper arm (over the deltoid), not the little finger.
feedback.ur: C5 outer upper arm (deltoid ke upar) hota hai, little finger nahi.

feedback.en: C6 is thumb and index finger — the opposite side of the hand.
feedback.ur: C6 thumb aur index finger hai — haath ki doosri side.

title.ur: Sensation sahi tareeqay se kaise test karein

steps.title: Explain and show first
steps.detail: Touch the patient's sternum with the cotton wool or pin so they know what "normal" feels like. Then ask them to close their eyes. || Pehle samjhayein aur dikhayein

steps.title: Test the key point, not the whole skin
steps.detail: Use the standard key point for each level (for C6, the thumb; for L5, the top of the foot at the 3rd MTP joint). Touch lightly and briefly, never stroking. || Poori skin nahi, key point test karein

steps.title: Compare left with right
steps.detail: Ask "Does this feel the same as here?" while touching the matching point on the other side. A difference between sides is more reliable than any single answer. || Left ko right se compare karein

steps.title: Test two modalities
steps.detail: Light touch (cotton wool) and pinprick (a new neurotip or safety pin, ask "sharp or blunt?"). They travel in different tracts, so testing both helps you localise. || Do modalities test karein

steps.title: Randomise and never lead
steps.detail: Vary the order and the pauses, and don't say "now?" before every touch. A patient who is guessing will be right 50% of the time, so test several points. || Tarteeb badalte rahein aur leading na karein

beats.title: L5 dermatome — top of the foot and big toe

intro.en: Now the leg. The **L5 zone** runs down the outer shin, over the top of the foot to the big toe. Test at the 3rd metatarsophalangeal joint, then slide to **S1** on the outer edge of the foot and compare.
intro.ur: Ab taang. **L5 zone** outer shin se foot ke top par hota hua bare angootay tak jati hai. 3rd metatarsophalangeal joint par test karein, phir **S1** (foot ka bahar wala kinara) par ja kar compare karein.

text.en: The commonest mistakes: pressing the pin too hard (it becomes a pain test, not a sensation test), testing only one side, asking leading questions, and trusting a vague answer. Another trap is testing right after the patient has been scratched, hot or cold — skin that was rubbed feels different.
text.ur: Aam ghaltiyan: pin zor se dabana (yeh sensation test nahi, dard ka test ban jata hai), sirf ek side test karna, leading sawal poochna, aur mubham jawab par bharosa karna. Ek aur jaal: patient ko khujane, garmi ya sardi ke foran baad test karna — ragri hui skin ka ehsaas alag hota hai.

rows.en: A strip following the root map, often with matching pain
rows.ur: Root map ki patti, aksar dard ke saath
Nerve root ka masla (disc, stenosis, shingles)

rows.en: A patch that fits one nerve's territory (e.g. little + half ring finger)
rows.ur: Ek nerve ke territory jaisa patch (maslan little + aadhi ring finger)

rows.en: Entrapment or injury of that nerve (e.g. ulnar at the elbow)
rows.ur: Us nerve ka entrapment ya injury (maslan elbow par ulnar)

rows.en: Symmetrical loss that starts in the toes and fingers and creeps upward
rows.ur: Dono sides barabar kami jo toes aur fingers se shuru ho kar upar charhti hai
Peripheral neuropathy (diabetes, B12 ki kami, sharab)

question.en: A man has reduced pinprick over the **outer shin, top of the foot and big toe** on the right, with weak toe extension. Which level, and which disc is the classic culprit?
question.ur: Aadmi ki right side par **outer shin, foot ke top aur bare angootay** par pinprick kam hai aur toe extension kamzor hai. Kaun sa level, aur classic wajah kaun si disc?

text.en: L5 root — usually an L4–L5 disc (traversing root)
text.ur: L5 root — aam taur par L4–L5 disc (traversing root)

feedback.en: Yes. Lumbar discs usually hit the root that is passing by (the traversing root), so L4–L5 compresses L5.
feedback.ur: Haan. Lumbar discs aam taur par guzarti hui (traversing) root ko dabati hain, is liye L4–L5 L5 ko dabati hai.

feedback.en: S1 gives numbness on the outer foot and heel and weak plantarflexion. The big toe and top of the foot are L5.
feedback.ur: S1 outer foot aur heel ko sunn karti hai aur plantarflexion kamzor karti hai. Bara angootha aur foot ka top L5 hain.

feedback.en: L3 is the inner thigh and knee area; it would not reach the foot.
feedback.ur: L3 inner thigh aur knee ka area hai; woh foot tak nahi pohnchti.

text.en: In practice, record the findings as a map (draw the area on a body chart) and write the levels: "Reduced light touch and pinprick R L5 dermatome, normal S1". In spinal cord injury the ISNCSCI exam scores 28 key points on each side, 0–2 for light touch and pinprick (maximum 112 each), and the **sensory level** is the lowest level that is normal on both.
text.ur: Practice mein findings ko map ki shakal mein likhein (body chart par area draw karein) aur levels likhein: “R L5 dermatome mein light touch aur pinprick kam, S1 normal”. Spinal cord injury mein ISNCSCI exam har side ke 28 key points ko 0–2 se score karta hai (light touch aur pinprick, har ek ka maximum 112) aur **sensory level** woh sabse neechla level hai jo dono mein normal ho.

text.en: Dermatome maps are an **average**: neighbouring dermatomes overlap, and the textbook maps (Foerster, Keegan–Garrett, Lee) differ from one another. Because of overlap, a single root lesion often causes a smaller patch of numbness than the map suggests — and pain is usually felt in a wider area than the numbness. Hence the rule: combine the sensory finding with **weakness and reflexes** before naming the root.
text.ur: Dermatome maps ek **average** hain: qareeb ke dermatomes overlap karte hain, aur textbook maps (Foerster, Keegan–Garrett, Lee) ek doosre se mukhtalif hain. Overlap ki wajah se single root lesion aksar map se chhota sunn patch deti hai — aur dard aam taur par sunn area se zyada phaila hota hai. Is liye qaida: root ka naam lene se pehle sensory finding ko **kamzori aur reflexes** ke saath milayein.

question.en: Why does a patient with a compressed L5 root often have only a small patch of numbness on the foot, not the whole L5 ribbon?
question.ur: Dabi hui L5 root wale patient ke foot par aksar sirf chhota sa sunn patch kyun hota hai, poori L5 ribbon kyun nahi?

answer.en: Because neighbouring roots (L4 and S1) also supply part of the same skin, so the area supplied by L5 **alone** (the autonomous zone, e.g. the web between the first and second toes) is small. Always test the autonomous zone.
answer.ur: Kyunke qareeb ki roots (L4 aur S1) bhi usi skin ke kuch hissay ko supply karti hain, is liye sirf L5 se supply hone wala area (autonomous zone, maslan pehli aur doosri toe ke beech ka web) chhota hota hai. Hamesha autonomous zone test karein.

question.en: Which tool detects **loss of protective sensation** in a diabetic foot?
question.ur: Diabetic foot mein **protective sensation ki kami** kaun sa tool pakarta hai?

text.en: A 10 g monofilament pressed on standard sites on the sole
text.ur: Sole ke standard sites par 10 g monofilament dabana

feedback.en: Yes. If the patient cannot feel it at several sites, protective sensation is lost and the ulcer risk is high — teach daily foot checks.
feedback.ur: Haan. Agar patient kayi sites par mehsoos na kare to protective sensation chali gayi hai aur ulcer ka khatra zyada hai — roz foot check sikhayein.

text.en: A cotton ball on the shin

feedback.en: Light touch on the shin is too coarse and in the wrong place; the sole sites are standard.
feedback.ur: Shin par light touch bohat mota test hai aur ghalat jagah par; sole ke sites standard hain.

text.en: A tuning fork on the knee

feedback.en: A 128 Hz fork tests vibration, but on a bony toe or ankle, not the knee.
feedback.ur: 128 Hz fork vibration test karti hai, lekin knee par nahi, toe ya ankle ki haddi par.

text.en: **Stop and refer urgently** if you find numbness around the saddle area (genitals, anus, inner thighs), new bladder or bowel changes, or progressive weakness in both legs. These suggest cauda equina syndrome or cord compression and need same-day emergency assessment.
text.ur: **Foran refer karein** agar saddle area (genitals, anus, inner thighs) mein numbness, bladder ya bowel mein nayi tabdeeli, ya dono taangon mein barhti hui kamzori ho. Yeh cauda equina syndrome ya cord compression ka ishara hain aur usi din emergency assessment chahiye.

summary.en: A dermatome is the skin strip of one root: test the key point, compare both sides, use light touch and pinprick, and never lead the patient.
summary.ur: Dermatome ek root ki skin patti hai: key point test karein, dono sides compare karein, light touch aur pinprick use karein, aur patient ko leading na karein.

summary.en: Name the root by combining numbness with weakness and reflexes — overlap makes the map approximate, so test the autonomous zone.
summary.ur: Root ka naam sunn area ke saath kamzori aur reflexes ko mila kar lein — overlap map ko andaza bana deta hai, is liye autonomous zone test karein.

summary.en: Read the pattern: dermatomal strip = root, nerve territory = peripheral nerve, glove-and-stocking = neuropathy; saddle numbness is an emergency.
summary.ur: Pattern parhein: dermatomal patti = root, nerve territory = peripheral nerve, glove-and-stocking = neuropathy; saddle numbness emergency hai.

front.en: Which fingers does C6, C7 and C8 supply?
front.ur: C6, C7 aur C8 kaun si fingers ko supply karti hain?

back.en: C6 thumb + index, C7 middle finger, C8 little finger (the "6-7-8" hand trick).
back.ur: C6 thumb + index, C7 middle finger, C8 little finger (“6-7-8” hand trick).

back.en: The top of the foot at the 3rd metatarsophalangeal joint (dorsum of the foot).
back.ur: Foot ka top, 3rd metatarsophalangeal joint par (dorsum of the foot).

front.en: Why test both light touch and pinprick?
front.ur: Light touch aur pinprick dono kyun test karte hain?

back.en: They travel in different tracts (dorsal column vs spinothalamic), so a difference between them helps localise a lesion.
back.ur: Yeh alag tracts (dorsal column vs spinothalamic) se guzarti hain, is liye dono ka farq lesion localise karne mein madad deta hai.

front.en: What is the sensory level in ISNCSCI?
front.ur: ISNCSCI mein sensory level kya hota hai?

back.en: The most caudal (lowest) dermatome with normal (score 2) light touch and pinprick on that side.
back.ur: Sab se neechla (caudal) dermatome jis mein us side par light touch aur pinprick normal (score 2) hon.

front.en: Which tool checks protective sensation in the diabetic foot?
front.ur: Diabetic foot mein protective sensation kaun sa tool check karta hai?

back.en: A 10 g (5.07) Semmes–Weinstein monofilament at standard plantar sites.
back.ur: Standard plantar sites par 10 g (5.07) Semmes–Weinstein monofilament.

note.en: Practise every key point and take the level tests.
note.ur: Har key point practise karein aur level tests dein.

note.en: Pair the sensory exam with reflexes and tone.
note.ur: Sensory exam ko reflexes aur tone ke saath jorein.
